facts.fact: Rendering with view_layer.use_pass_cryptomatte_object on writes CryptoObject00-02 layers and adds those outputs to the Render Layers node; a new Cryptomatte node starts with these settings
layer_name is a dynamic enum: the registered items say 'CryptoObject', 'CryptoMaterial', 'CryptoAsset', but the node only takes '<view layer>.CryptoObject' and so on; the plain name raises TypeError
facts.error: bpy_struct: item.attr = val: enum "CryptoObject" not found in ('ViewLayer.CryptoObject', 'ViewLayer.CryptoMaterial')

facts.fact: cm.matte_id = 'CubeB' (the object's name) pulled CubeB's matte in a background render: 1.0 inside the object, 0 outside; thresholded at 0.5 it agreed with the Object Index pass on every pixel, and edge pixels just outside the index mask held partial coverage (anti-aliasing, up to 0.375). The node's Image output is the render with alpha multiplied by the matte; cm.entries lists the names
Several objects: matte_id is a comma-separated list; 'CubeA,CubeC' and 'CubeA, CubeC' gave the same matte
A name that matches no object gives an all-zero matte and no error
layer_name = 'ViewLayer.CryptoMaterial' with a material name pulls the objects using that material
The same node pulls the matte from an EEVEE render; EEVEE writes no Object Index pass, so the check uses the Cycles render's index
